title: House Swapping
statementMd:
*Home? What is that? I see houses.*

— GePeTo

In order to teach people empathy, GePeTo demands that people often change houses, so that they learn to "live in another's shoes". There are $N$ houses in the city, each housing one person, and on the $i$-th house GePeTo placed the label $\pi(i)$ meaning that, every day at midnight, the person living in house $i$ has to move to house $\pi(i)$. All people move at the same time, and it is guaranteed that after a move no house is left empty, and no house has two people.

We say $\pi$ has a cycle of size $k$ if, after $k$ days, some person returns to the house where they initially lived, that is, if $\pi^k(x) = x$ for some $1 \leq x \leq N$.

GePeTo asks you to swap the labels of two houses in order to maximize the size of the smallest cycle, that is, choose a single pair $(i, j)$ and swap $\pi(i)$ with $\pi(j)$ to maximize the minimum $k$ such that $\pi^k(x) = x$ for some $1 \leq x \leq N$. You are allowed to choose $j = i$, in which case $\pi$ remains unchanged.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1 \leq T \leq 10^5$), the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of two lines. The first line contains an integer $N$ ($2 \leq N \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$), the number of houses. The second line contains $N$ distinct integers between $1$ and $N$, the $i$-th being $\pi(i)$. The sum of $N$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, print a line with three integers $k$, $i$, and $j$ ($1 \leq k, i, j \leq N$), such that the maximum size of the minimum cycle is $k$ after swapping positions $i$ and $j$. If there are multiple answers, any valid answer will be accepted.
